title: Roots and end behaviour
steps: The zeros are \(-4,1,3\), so the factors are \((x+4)(x-1)(x-3)\). The right-hand end rises, requiring a positive leading coefficient.

title: Mode of a continuous distribution
steps: The mode is the horizontal coordinate where the density is greatest. The highest point occurs at \(x=2\sqrt2\), rather than at the height \(\sqrt2/2\).

title: Horizontal stretch and reflection
steps: The domain doubles from \([0,4]\) to \([0,8]\), giving \(f(x/2)\). The heights change sign, so reflect in the horizontal axis.

title: Interpreting correlation
steps: A positive correlation describes a tendency for both variables to increase together. It does not establish causation or mean that 62% of students follow a particular pattern.
answer: D: students who study more tend to score higher.

title: Rise above the launch point
steps: The starting height is \(h(0)=45\). At the maximum, \(h(3)=45+36-18=63\), so the rise is \(63-45\).

title: The ambiguous sine-rule case
steps: The sine rule gives the whole obtuse angle at G as \(180^\circ-68.3^\circ=111.7^\circ\). The dashed perpendicular already accounts for \(55^\circ\), leaving \(111.7^\circ-55^\circ=56.7^\circ\) on the right.

title: Sum of two independent rolls
steps: The ordered pairs giving a sum of \(-3\) are \((-4,1),(1,-4),(-3,0),(0,-3)\). Multiply within each independent pair, then add.

title: Odd functions and signed areas
steps: Let \(A\) be the positive area from 0 to 1 and \(B\) the magnitude of the smaller negative area from 1 to a. Then \(A>B>0\). Odd symmetry gives \(P=A-B\), \(Q=0\), \(S=-P\), and \(R=-P+A=B\).
The diagram also shows \(A>2B\), so \(R<P\). Thus \(S<Q<R<P\).

title: Combining normal tails
steps: By symmetry, \(P(Z>1.2)=P(Z<-1.2)\). Split the latter at \(-1.5\), then add the left tail.

title: Range of a composite function
steps: Put \(u=\sin x\), so \(-1\le u\le1\). Complete the square: \(u^2-u=(u-1/2)^2-1/4\). The minimum is \(-1/4\) at \(u=1/2\); the maximum is 2 at \(u=-1\).

title: Gradient of a tangent
steps: Differentiate to obtain \(y\prime=3x^2+3\), then substitute \(x=-1\).

title: Interquartile range
steps: Exclude the middle (seventh) value, 22, when forming the lower and upper halves. Their medians are \(Q_1=(15+17)/2=16\) and \(Q_3=(27+28)/2=27.5\).

title: Upper outlier fence
steps: The upper fence is \(Q_3+1.5\,\mathrm{IQR}=27.5+1.5(11.5)=44.75\). The lower fence is \(-1.25\), below the smallest observation. Because m counts cars, it is an integer.

title: Finding an arithmetic sequence
steps: With first term a and common difference d, \(a+2d=30\) and \(a+5d=42\). Subtracting gives \(3d=12\), so \(d=4\) and \(a=30-8\).

title: Summing the seats
steps: Use \(S_n=\frac n2[2a+(n-1)d]\) with \(a=22,d=4,n=9\).

title: Range and period
steps: Since \(-1\le\cos(2x)\le1\), multiplying by 3 and adding 1 gives \(-2\le h(x)\le4\). The angular multiplier 2 halves the usual cosine period.

title: Differentiating an exponential composite
steps: For \(a^{u(x)}\), the derivative is \(a^{u(x)}\ln(a)u\prime(x)\). Here \(u=x^2+3\), so \(u\prime=2x\).

title: Reading a scatterplot
steps: Read the vertical coordinate of the lowest plotted point. It lies just above 6.0, at 6.1.

title: Interpreting a regression slope
steps: The slope compares the predicted change in the public’s score with a one-unit increase in the critics’ score.
answer: For each extra point in the critics’ score, the predicted public score increases by 0.54 points on average.

title: Adding a point to a regression
steps: The new point is below the fitted line and to the left of the data centre. It pulls the left end of the fitted line downward, making the positive slope steeper.

title: Interpreting the decay factor
steps: A factor of 0.8 means that each year the maximum capacity is 80% of its value one year earlier.
answer: The maximum storage capacity falls by 20% per year.

title: Intersections of a line and parabola
steps: Equate the two formulas: \(7-3x=-x^2+x+12\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-4x-5=(x-5)(x+1)=0\).

title: Area between two curves
steps: The parabola is above the line between the intersections, so integrate their difference.

title: Sketching a derivative
steps: The original curve decreases up to \(x=2\), so the derivative starts below the axis. It is zero at the local minimum and positive afterwards.

The slope is greatest at the inflection point \(x=5\), giving a local maximum of \(f\prime\). The slope then decreases towards 0 from above as f approaches its horizontal asymptote. The vertical scale is not specified.
answer: A curve crossing at \(x=2\), peaking above the axis at \(x=5\), then approaching \(y=0\) from above.

title: Multiplying along a probability tree
steps: Follow the walk branch and then the incorrect-uniform branch: \(\frac3{10}\times\frac1{10}\).

title: At least one success
steps: Using the independent-selection model intended by the tree, the probability a student does not meet both conditions is \(1-0.03=0.97\). Subtract the probability neither student does from 1.

title: Quotient rule with a logarithm
steps: Apply the quotient rule, keeping the entire denominator squared.

title: Checking endpoints for a global maximum
steps: The stationary point is \(x=e\). The derivative changes from negative to positive there, so it is a minimum.
Compare the endpoint values: \(g(2)=2/\ln2\approx2.885\), while \(g(5)=5/\ln5\approx3.107\).
answer: The global maximum is \(5/\ln5\approx3.107\), attained at \(x=5\).

title: Rewriting a rational function
steps: Split the numerator as \(x+2=(x+1)+1\), then divide each term by \(x+1\).

title: Translating a reciprocal graph
steps: Replacing x by \(x+1\) shifts \(y=1/x\) left by one unit. Adding 1 shifts it up by one unit.
answer: Translate one unit left and one unit up.

title: Bearings, area and the cosine rule
steps: Write \(OA=OB=r\). The area formula gives \(80=\tfrac12 r^2\sin45^\circ\), so \(r=\sqrt{160/\sin45^\circ}\approx15.0424\text{ km}\).
The included angle \(BOC=253^\circ-101^\circ=152^\circ\). Apply the cosine rule: \(BC=\sqrt{r^2+25^2-2r(25)\cos152^\circ}\approx38.93\text{ km}\).

title: Finding a continuous decay constant
steps: If 75% has decayed, 25% remains: \(250=1000e^{10.54k}\). Taking logarithms gives \(k=\ln(0.25)/10.54\).

title: Time from a decay rate
steps: Differentiate to get \(A\prime(t)=1000k e^{kt}\). Set this to \(-9.48\) and use the unrounded value \(k=\ln(0.25)/10.54\).
\[t=\frac{\ln\!\left(\frac{-9.48}{1000k}\right)}{k}\approx19.996.\]

title: Normal symmetry about the mean
steps: The upper boundary is \(5.89-4.82=1.07\) kg above the mean, exactly matching the distance \(4.82-3.75=1.07\) kg below it. Symmetry makes the upper tail probability 0.116.
The area from the mean to the upper boundary is therefore \(0.5-0.116\).

title: Direction changes from velocity
steps: Solve \(1-e^{\cos(\pi t)}=0\), giving \(\cos(\pi t)=0\). Only \(t=0.5\) lies in the given interval; velocity changes from negative to positive there.

title: Acceleration using the chain rule
steps: Differentiating velocity gives \(a(t)=\pi e^{\cos(\pi t)}\sin(\pi t)\). At \(t=0.5\), the exponential factor and sine factor are both 1.

title: Trapezoidal estimate of distance
steps: Distance integrates speed, so use the absolute values of the velocities. The sign change is at a table point, allowing the trapezoidal rule to be applied across both pieces.

title: Changing annuity contributions
steps: The half-yearly rate is \(i=0.01\), and there are 10 end-of-period payments. Let \(s_n=((1.01)^n-1)/0.01\). Paying $750 throughout gives \(750s_{10}\). Doubling the last m payments adds a further \(750s_m\).
Thus \(750(10.4622+s_m)\ge14000\), or \(s_m\ge8.20447\). The table gives \(s_8=8.2857\), so eight doubled payments suffice.
Seven doubled payments give \(s_7\approx7.2135\), which is too small. Therefore at least eight of the ten payments must be $1500.

title: Three distinct cubic roots
steps: Differentiate: \(y\prime=12x^2-6x-6=6(2x+1)(x-1)\). The stationary points occur at \(x=-1/2\) and \(x=1\).
The derivative signs \(+,-,+\) show a local maximum at \(-1/2\) with height \(d+7/4\), and a local minimum at 1 with height \(d-5\).
For three distinct crossings, the maximum must be strictly positive and the minimum strictly negative: \(d+7/4>0\) and \(d-5<0\). Equality would give a repeated root and only two intercepts.

title: Sketching the cotangent graph
steps: Use \(\cot x=\cos x/\sin x\). It has vertical asymptotes at \(x=0,\pi,2\pi\) and zeros at \(x=\pi/2,3\pi/2\).
Each branch decreases from \(+\infty\) to \(-\infty\) between successive asymptotes. Neither endpoint is in the domain.

title: Domain of a logarithmic composite
steps: The logarithm needs \(\cot x>0\). Sine and cosine have the same sign in the first and third quadrants. Exclude both zeros of cotangent and its asymptotes.

title: Derivative of log cotangent
steps: Use the chain rule and \((\cot x)\prime=-\csc^2x\).
\[\frac{d}{dx}\ln(\cot x)=\frac{-\csc^2x}{\cot x}=-\frac{1}{\sin x\cos x}=-\csc x\sec x.\]
answer: \(-\csc x\sec x\), wherever \(\ln(\cot x)\) is defined.

title: Pyramid volume in terms of an angle
steps: In the right triangle AOM, the height is \(MO=\ell\sin\theta\) and the half-diagonal of the square is \(AO=\ell\cos\theta\).
The square’s full diagonal is \(2\ell\cos\theta\), so its area is half the diagonal squared: \(2\ell^2\cos^2\theta\). Multiply base area by height and divide by 3.

title: Optimising the pyramid volume
steps: For fixed \(\ell>0\), differentiate the angle-dependent factor: \(V\prime=\frac{2\ell^3}{3}\cos\theta(1-3\sin^2\theta)\).

For a non-degenerate pyramid, \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), so the interior stationary point satisfies \(\sin\theta=1/\sqrt3\). The derivative is positive before this angle and negative after it, giving the maximum.

title: Integrating a cosine
steps: The derivative of \(\sin(2x)\) is \(2\cos(2x)\), so divide by 2.

title: Recovering a positive function
steps: Since f is positive, \(\int f\prime(x)/f(x)\,dx=\ln f(x)\). Hence \(\ln f(x)=\tfrac12\sin(2x)+C\).
Use \(f(0)=1\) to obtain \(C=0\), then exponentiate.

title: Definite integral with a variable bound
steps: Apply the fundamental theorem using \(F\prime(t)=\sqrt{\tan t}\). Evaluate F at the upper bound and subtract its value at the lower bound.

title: Differentiating a variable lower bound
steps: The term \(F(1)\) is constant. Differentiate \(-F(x^3)\) by the chain rule, then substitute \(F\prime(x^3)=\sqrt{\tan(x^3)}\).

title: Loan balance after three repayments
steps: Write \(r=1.005\) for monthly interest and \(q=1.1\) for payment growth. The first three balances are \(A_1=83000r-760\), \(A_2=83000r^2-760r-760q\), and \(A_3=83000r^3-760r^2-760qr-760q^2\).

title: Summing increasing loan repayments
steps: After n repayments, \(A_n=83000r^n-760\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}r^{n-1-j}q^j\), where \(r=1.005\) and \(q=1.1\).
The geometric sum equals \((q^n-r^n)/(q-r)\). Since \(760/(1.1-1.005)=8000\), simplify to \(83000r^n-8000(q^n-r^n)\).

title: The final loan repayment
steps: The scheduled formula first reaches a non-positive balance when \(n\ge\ln(91000/8000)/\ln(1.1/1.005)\approx26.919\). Thus 26 full repayments are made and the final payment is in month 27.

The amount owing after repayment 26 is \(A_{26}=91000(1.005)^{26}-8000(1.1)^{26}\approx8254.41\). Add one month’s interest rather than paying the full scheduled 27th instalment: \(1.005A_{26}\approx8295.68\).
